findings.title: Audit across service boundaries
findings.requirement: Rebuild a run across the gateway, tool services, and delegated workers, with all six identity fields kept. Check that the agent can't erase or rewrite its audit history, either directly or by asking a more powerful tool or peer. Check that a vendor boundary doesn't leave any action untraceable to the agent and instance that did it.

Authorization decisions missing the policy version in the run record
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies

evidence.note: Audit rows carry all six fields in the gateway and the in-process extractor sub-agent, but outbound calls to the ERP gateway send no trace context (only run_id/business_unit in _meta, mcp_client.py:125), and pay_invoice sends no trace header (payments.py:31). No httpx/OTel instrumentation is installed (pyproject.toml). The mail ingest write (ingest.py:142) and the approval decision (main.py:183) write no audit row. Tool services themselves are outside this repo.

checks.check: Calls into vendor services are mapped from the gateway's verified identity and correlation ID to the vendor's job or receipt ID.
checks.verify: 1) Find calls into vendor services. 2) Check the gateway stores its verified identity and correlation ID together with the vendor's job or receipt ID. 3) Answer no if the vendor ID is not stored, or stored without the link to identity and correlation ID.

checks.note: On success tool_result stores the vendor payment_id/PO result beside operation_id, tenant, instance and trace_id (loop.py:95-100). On any exception after the vendor call (30s timeout, bad response body) tool_error stores only the exception type and message, no vendor id, and pay_invoice's Idempotency-Key (payments.py:33) is not stored. A vendor action can exist with no vendor receipt linked to the agent instance. Generic erp_call results are stored as returned, with no guaranteed job id.

violates: Check that a vendor boundary doesn't leave any action untraceable to the agent and instance that did it
findings.summary: Agent and sub-agent audit rows keep all six fields and the agent cannot edit them, but vendor segments are not joined by trace context and failed vendor calls store no receipt id.
findings.next_step: Send traceparent and a correlation id to ERP and payments, store the vendor id or idempotency key on every outcome including errors, and audit mail ingest and approval decisions.

findings.title: Protect shared evidence
findings.requirement: Set rules for how long audit records are kept, who can see them, what is redacted, how their integrity is checked, and how they are exported and restored. Test pulling up a past run, and test that missing records or a broken pipeline get noticed. Keep records long enough for investigations and for the law. For example, the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers of high-risk systems to keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (Articles 19 and 26). High-impact actions must fail closed when required audit capture isn't working.

not_covered.problem: Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Run record missing denials, approvals, or results
Secrets left in tool output, responses, or normal logs

evidence.note: digest() hashes single payloads (result_sha256, args) but audit rows have no prev-hash chain, signature, sequence number or delivery receipt (audit_events columns 001_init.sql:4-27). Nothing verifies a hash. No alert on gaps or pipeline failure anywhere in the repo. Grants make the table insert-only for the agent, which is not WORM or tamper evidence.

findings.title: Fleet incident response
findings.requirement: Run a drill where a shared tool or agent type is compromised. Find the affected instances and tenants. Quarantine the dependency, revoke the access involved, stop affected work, and alert the named responders. Check that alerts about abuse across agents, and about budgets, reach the team that can act. Name who decides whether to report outside the organization and share information.

not_covered.problem: Kill switch for a single agent not drilled
No owner named on each side of a shared control
Tool or MCP server approved without vetting or pinning
Budget and rate limits not enforced outside the model

evidence.note: killswitch.assert_running is called once at run start; running work is not re-checked
halt scopes are only 'fleet' or one tenant; no tool or agent-type quarantine
only alert is a budget message to one Slack channel; no cross-agent abuse alert or named responder

red_flags_found: app/loop.py:127 Halt is only read once at run start and scopes are only fleet or tenant, so a compromised tool or agent type cannot be quarantined and running work is not stopped
violates: Quarantine the dependency, revoke the access involved, stop affected work
findings.summary: The only stop control is a fleet or tenant halt checked at run start; there is no tool or agent-type quarantine, no fleet impact query, and the only alert is one Slack channel for budgets.
findings.next_step: Add tool and agent-type quarantine checked on every step, a query from tool version to instances and tenants, abuse alerts to a named on-call, and a runbook naming who decides on outside reporting.
